Independent bounded reproduction: for each 3<=d<=12 and 1<=k<=d, minimize the k-by-k assignment cost by the partial-sink-mask recurrence D(S union {j})=min(D(S union {j}),D(S)+c(|S|,j)), with diagonal cost 2 and off-diagonal cost sqrt(2). Multiply by a-b and divide by 2 sqrt(k)/d; compare the result with the two mixed-pair costs and the closed formula. Maxima at d=3,6,12 were 1.172211621632336, 1.333052557189806, 1.391596983136669, respectively, tied between the incident and antipodal constraints.
correctness.rationale: Averaging over signed permutations reduces every finite-norm extension, even a signed one, to incident and opposite weights a=1/d-b and b. The distance-to-an-incident-vertex test bounds the norm below by A(b)=sqrt(2(d-1)/d)+2b/r, and the two-level test on antipodal facets bounds it below by sqrt(d/2)|1-2db|. For d>=3 the increasing and decreasing affine bounds meet at a strictly positive b*<1/(2d), and their maximum bounds every real b from below by the intersection value. For these positive weights, the mixed pair with an opposite vertex is no worse than the incident pair: at b=0 the comparison is 1<=(2-sqrt(2))(d-1), and increasing b only improves it. For a k-coordinate sign change, cancel the equal masses. If k=1 the only transport costs 2(a-b); otherwise each remaining cross-distance is at least sqrt(2), attained in all k matches by a cyclic permutation of the changed coordinates. Thus the centroid-pair maximum is achieved at k=d, including comparison with k=1. Substitution gives the stated formula, which exceeds 1, is strictly below ordinary averaging, and tends to sqrt(2).

value.rationale: Facet centroids give a canonical family in every dimension, with a genuinely simultaneous obstruction. Ordinary averaging on just the incident vertices is sufficient for a strictly smaller one-centroid norm, but treating every facet at once forces a competition with antipodal centroid differences. The exact result quantifies this cost and shows how strictly positive mass on all vertices improves the simultaneous norm from order sqrt(d) to a bounded constant.
residual_risks: No conclusion about uniqueness, other augmentation sets or other metrics.
